ALTERNATIVE METHODS
The City provides the following two alternative methods of viewing and listening to the City Council Meeting
convenience:

  ¡  On Spectrum Cable Channel 35 with audio and limited video. Please check with your cable provider
  for details.
  ¡  Live online through Facebook Live, with audio and limited video,
  at https://www.facebook.com/cityofinglewood/

The disruption in service of any alternative method does not preclude the City Council or other legislative body
from taking further action on an agenda item.

Submitting Comments Prior to Public Meeting: Members of the public may choose to submit comments
electronically for consideration by the City Council or other City Legislative Body by sending them to the City
Clerk/Secretary at athompson@cityofinglewood.org, and Deputy City Clerk at aallen@cityofinglewood.org. To
ensure distribution to the members of the Legislative Body prior to consideration of the agenda, please submit
comments prior to 8:00 a.m. the day of the meeting, and in the body of the email, please identify the agenda
number or subject matter. Correspondence should indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments receiv
after 8:00 a.m. and prior to the close of the public hearings will be made part of the official public record of the
meeting. Contact the Office of the City Clerk at 310-412-5280 with any questions.

ACCESSIBILITY: If requested, the agenda and backup materials will be made available in appropriate
 comments prior to 8:00 a.m. the day of the meeting, and in the body of the email, please identify the agenda
number or subject matter. Correspondence should indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments receiv
after 8:00 a.m. and prior to the close of the public hearings will be made part of the official public record of the
meeting. Contact the Office of the City Clerk at 310-412-5280 with any questions.

ACCESSIBILITY: If requested, the agenda and backup materials will be made available in appropriate
alternative formats to persons with a disability, as required by Section 202 of the Americans with Disabilities A
1990 (42 U.S.C. Sec. 12132), and the federal rules and regulations adopted in implementation thereof. Any
person who requires a disability-related modification or accommodation, or translation services in order to observe
and/or offer public comment may request such reasonable modification, accommodation, or service by contact
the Office of the City Clerk by telephone at 310-412-5280,  FAX at 310 -412-5533, One Manchester
Boulevard, First Floor, Inglewood City Hall, Inglewood, CA 90301 or via email
to athompson@cityofinglewood.org and aallen@cityofinglewood.org no later than 24 hours prior to the scheduled
meeting.

Inglewood, California
  January 23, 2024

The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
January 23, 2024, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

Mayor Butts called the City Council into Closed Session at the hour of 1:02 p.m.

The City Clerk announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present: Mayor Butts, Council Members Morales, and Faulk; and
  Absent: Council Members Gray, and Padilla.

City officials and personnel present for Closed Session were as follows:

  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk
  Mark F. Weinberg  City Manager
  Ken Campos  City Attorney
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING CLOSED SESSION ITEMS. Mayor Butts
inquired if there were any persons present who wished to address the City Council on the
Closed Session Item Nos. CS-1, CS-2, CS-3, and CS-4.

There was no response.

Mayor Butts recessed the City Council at the hour of 1:02 p.m. for Closed Session Item
Nos. CS-1, CS-2, CS-3, and CS-4.

  *****************

Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the City
Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, Parking
Authority, and Joint Powers Authority at the hour of 2:00 p.m.
The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary/Parking
Authority Secretary/Joint Powers Authority Secretary announced the presence of a quorum
as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman/Parking Authority Chairman/ Joint Powers
  Authority Chairman Butts, Council Members/Successor
  Agency Members/Housing Authority Members/Parking
  Authority Members/ Joint Powers Authority Members
  Gray, Morales, Faulk; and
  Absent:  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing
  Authority Member/Parking Authority Member/Joint
  Powers Authority Member Padilla.
City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Parking Authority/ Joint Powers Authority
officials and personnel present were as follows:
  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Mark F. Weinberg  City Manager/ Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Louis Atwell  Assistant City Manager/Public Works Director
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

* Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, Parking Authority, and
Joint Powers Authority.
 January 23, 2024

  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman/Parking Authority Chairman/ Joint Powers
  Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons present who wished to address
  the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Parking Authority/ Joint Powers
  Authority on any item on the Agendas, other than the Public Hearing.

  There was no response.

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member
  /Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Faulk that the
  demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated January
  18, 2024, in the amount of $7,281,913.40, and dated January 12, 2024, in the amount of
  $5,528,449.18,  are hereby allowed, and the City Clerk/Successor Agency
  Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to certify upon said registers
  that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Gray, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Padilla.

301  PUBLIC HEARING HELD – AN APPEAL OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION
  DENIAL FOR SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO. 23-00017 (SUP23-00017);
  RESOLUTION NO. 24-28 ADOPTED – UPHOLDING THE PLANNING
  COMMISSION’S DENIAL OF SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO. SUP23-00017. The City
  Clerk announced the next scheduled matter was a public hearing to consider an appeal by
  J.D. Thompson (applicant) of the Planning Commission’s denial of Special Use Permit No.
  23-00017 to allow a mortuary in an approximately 4,200 square-foot one-story commercial
  building on an approximately 5,200 square-foot M-1 (Light Manufacturing) Zoned property
  at 323 East Beach Avenue, that notice was given in the time, form and manner as required
  by law, an affidavit was on file and communications were received and distributed to the
  Mayor and Council Members.

  The City Clerk, Aisha L. Thompson received communications via email from Gina Lamb
  and Steve Hurd, who favored the Planning Commission’s denial of Special Use Permit No.
  23-00017.

  Mayor Butts ordered the communications received and filed.

  Mark F. Weinberg, City Manager, presented the Staff Report dated January 23, 2024.

  Christopher Jackson, Sr., Development Services Director, gave a brief oral report regarding
  the Planning Commission’s denial of Special Use Permit No. 23-00017.

  Mayor Butts left the dais at the hour of 2:03 p.m.

  Mayor Butts returned to the dais at the hour of 2:04 p.m.

  Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present that wished to address the City
  Council on this matter.

  The following persons spoke in favor of the Planning Commission’s denial of Special Use
  Permit No. 23-00017:

  Ching Huong
  Bishop W.A. Garrett
  Craig Spriker
  Speaker (Name Unknown)
  Keith Walsh
  Gina Lamb
  Amber Tuggerson

  2
 January 23, 2024

  Ken Herbert
  Anita Gladden
  Bernadette Cooper
  Joyce Dalal
  Vincent Phan
  Steven (Last Name Unknown)
  Shauna Shay
  Speaker (Name Unknown)
  Brian (Last Name Unknown)
  Steve Hurd

  Council Member Morales left the dais at the hour of 2:47 p.m.

  Council Member Morales returned to the dais at the hour of 2:48 p.m.

  The following persons spoke in opposition to the Planning Commission’s denial of Special
  Use Permit No. 23-00017:

  J.D. Thompson
  Rob Carlin
  Chris Clawson
  Nancy Lamus
  Christopher Grundy
  Reverend Berry Reed

  Mayor Butts closed the public comment portion at the hour of 2:55 p.m.

  Following discussion, it was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Mayor
  Butts that the City Council does hereby: 1) Uphold the Planning Commission’s denial of
  Special Use Permit No. 23-00017 (SUP23-00017); and 2) Adopt Resolution No. 24-28
  entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA, UPHOLDING THE PLANNING COMMISSION’S DENIAL OF
  A CERTAIN SPECIAL USE PERMIT REQUEST TO J.D. THOMPSON, TO
  ALLOW A MORTUARY IN AN APPROXIMATELY 4,200 SQUARE-FOOT,
  ONE-STORY COMMERCIAL BUILDING ON AN APPROXIMATELY 5,200
  SQUARE-FOOT M-1 (LIGHT MANUFACTURING) ZONED PROPERTY
  LOCATED AT 323 EAST BEACH AVENUE

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Padilla.

  MINUTES. It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Faulk that the Minutes for the City Council Meetings held on November 14, 2023, and
  November 21, 2023, be approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None;
  Abstain: Council Member Gray; and
  Absent: Council Member Padilla.

  Mayor Butts pulled Agenda Item No. 6 from the Agenda for further discussion.

  3

  following:
  A. Reject Claim pursuant to Government Code, Section 913:
  1. Jason Batiste for alleged Personal Injury; Excessive Force (LASD) on April 19, 2023.

  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and

101  CONTRACT AWARDED AND AGREEMENT NO. 24-104 APPROVED –
  BUFFALO COMPUTER GRAPHICS (BCG); PAYMENT AUTHORIZED –

  Staff report dated January 23, 2024, was presented recommending that the Mayor and

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2023-24

  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Morales, and Faulk, and Mayor Butts;

132.9  CLOSED SESSION – PENDING LITIGATION – ELIZABETH GARCIA V. CITY
  OF INGLEWOOD; ET AL. Closed Session – Confidential – Attorney/Client Privileged;
  City Council Conference with Legal Counsel regarding pending litigation pursuant to
  Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(1); Elizabeth Garcia v. City of Inglewood; et al.;
  LASC Case No.: 22STCV10396.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Mayor Butts, that the City
  Council does hereby approve the request for settlement. The motion was carried by the
  following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Morales, and Faulk;
  Noes: Mayor Butts; and
  Absent: Council Member Padilla.
